newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Spread widens on soft naphtha.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Spread widens on soft naphtha.

text.p: The pressure on the spread between the two light distillates started to ease as the recent support in naphtha disappeared, traders said on Friday.
Naphtha April swaps fell 50 cents per barrel overnight to $23.30/$23.50, as buyers disappeared, traders said.
"There are alot of offers but no buyers in the East...naphtha is weakening," said one trader with a major oil company. "Most April requirements have already been covered."
Singapore fob naphtha prices have risen since early March by over $2.00 per barrel to around $25.50, opening the arbitrage window from the West.
Traders have yet to confirm any arbitrage ship fixtures but said there a few cargoes possibly heading eastwards, which could bear down on sentiment.
The gasoline-naphtha spread, which had dipped as low as $3.20 earlier this week, found relief from the weaker naphtha and firmer gasoline.
"It should hit $4.00 soon if naphtha keeps falling," a trader said.
Gasoline found support despite a U.S. major aggressively offering fob Singapore cargoes.

It sold two 92-octane unleaded cargoes at $28.10 and $27.90 per barrel lifting April 1-15 to a Dutch trader and a European major who has sold 550,000 barrels of gasoline in the past week. On Thursday, the grade was offered at $28.00.
"We have sold so much, we can afford to buy at these lower levels," said the European major.
